top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson; B036) rests on a first-order question: who bears the adjustment costs of trade exposure. The local-labour-market designs are transparent and have been replicated and attacked for about a decade. The sign and local concentration of the adjustment costs survived in qualified form, while long-run magnitude and shift-share identification remain debated. The citation should therefore credit evidence on exposure, employment, wages and adjustment, claim no effect size, and say openly that it does not rule on the origins of the task framework. Attribution is the tightest available, since the core programme is jointly authored by the three, and the cost of leaving out Katz and the task lineage is real but acceptable under a narrow citation. I weigh this on the substance of the evidence, not on the ten-member support count, much of which came from round-1 revisions. P002 (Helpman, Melitz; B034) is a mature, prize-worthy mechanism, but the priority questions involving Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum and the overlap with the 2008 prize cannot be settled from the supplied evidence. I rank it second, ahead of no award.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. No co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Helpman or Melitz is evident; my main co-authors (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach and others) are not credited on either proposal. I disclose a long committee overlap with other members (Hassler, Krusell, Ellingsen, Svensson) and an adjunct post at Chicago Booth. My field is corporate finance, not labour or trade. Conflicts are disclosed, not adjudicated.
